source: EventMate draft: generic party-planning suggestions. No prices, availability, venue sizes or cultural, ritual or religious claims. Not reviewed by event professionals.

wedding.title: Pick a two-colour palette and repeat it across decor, stationery and signage
wedding.note: A small palette keeps everything looking planned.

wedding.title: Photo wall of printed memories from the couple's journey
wedding.cost_note: low to moderate, depending on print size
wedding.note: Guests have something personal to look at while they wait.

wedding.title: A handwritten welcome note at each seat
wedding.note: Personal touches scale well to a mid-sized guest list.

wedding.title: Ask the caterer about a live counter where guests build their own plate
wedding.cost_note: moderate: depends on the caterer's quote
wedding.note: A build-your-own counter suits a meat-free menu.

wedding.title: Agree a rain or heat backup with the venue for any outdoor part
wedding.note: Outdoor parts need a plan for weather.

wedding.title: Ask the venue where elders can sit close to the entrance
wedding.note: A bigger crowd makes comfortable seating worth planning.

wedding.title: Photo prompts printed on small cards for guests to use
wedding.note: Gives guests something to do between formal moments.

wedding.title: Decor built from fabric, paper and lanterns instead of fresh flowers
wedding.note: Keeps the look rich when money is limited.

wedding.title: Name one friend or relative as the day-of contact for vendors
wedding.note: One person answering vendor questions keeps the day calm.

wedding.title: Garden-party feel with lanterns and low seating corners
wedding.cost_note: low to moderate, depending on rentals
wedding.note: A relaxed look that suits an open-air setting.

engagement_party.title: Soft pastel palette with one bold accent colour
engagement_party.note: An easy look to carry through decor and stationery.

engagement_party.title: Fairy lights along the entrance and the photo corner
engagement_party.note: Warm lighting makes a larger room feel intimate.

engagement_party.title: A table of questions about the couple for guests to answer
engagement_party.note: A light activity that helps guests from both families mix.

engagement_party.title: Ask the caterer how a meat-free menu can feel festive, for example with a live chaat counter
engagement_party.cost_note: moderate: depends on the caterer's quote
engagement_party.note: A vegetarian menu benefits from one show-piece counter.

engagement_party.title: Confirm the order of the evening with the host so speeches stay short
engagement_party.note: A fixed running order avoids long gaps.

engagement_party.title: Plan where gifts and cards will be kept safely during the evening
engagement_party.note: More guests means more gifts to look after.

engagement_party.title: Hand-painted name boards and table numbers
A short slideshow of the couple's photos on a loop
engagement_party.note: Works best where a screen can be seen clearly.

engagement_party.title: Lanterns and potted plants to soften the entrance
engagement_party.cost_note: low to moderate, depending on rentals

engagement_party.title: Agree a rain or shade backup for any outdoor corner
engagement_party.note: Outdoor corners need a weather plan.

birthday.title: Build the day around a favourite hobby or colour of the guest of honour
birthday.note: A single idea makes decor and games feel connected.

birthday.title: A simple scavenger hunt around the venue
birthday.note: Keeps a mid-sized group busy and mixing.

birthday.title: Table games and card games for the quieter guests
birthday.note: Gives guests who dislike loud games a place to settle.

birthday.title: Balloon arch in two or three colours
birthday.note: A cheap decoration with a strong first impression.

birthday.title: Ask the caterer for a small dessert round so the cake does not have to do everything
birthday.cost_note: moderate: depends on the caterer's quote
birthday.note: Gives guests more than one sweet moment.

birthday.title: Label dishes clearly so guests with food preferences can choose with confidence
birthday.note: Clear labels help when diets differ.

birthday.title: Plan a weather-aware backup for the games if the venue is outdoors
birthday.note: Outdoor games depend on the weather.

birthday.title: Decide who cuts the cake and when, so the schedule has a fixed moment for it
birthday.note: A fixed cake moment keeps photos and speeches organised.

birthday.title: A memory jar where guests drop a note for the guest of honour
birthday.note: A keepsake the guest of honour can read later.

birthday.title: Photo corner with a simple backdrop and props
birthday.note: A small corner that guests use all evening.

corporate.title: A simple brand-colour palette on name cards and signage
corporate.note: Consistent colours look organised without extra spending.

corporate.title: A short icebreaker round at the start so teams mix
corporate.note: Helps people from different teams talk early.

corporate.title: Share the agenda and dress code with attendees ahead of time
Ask the caterer for a lighter lunch option so the afternoon session stays lively
corporate.cost_note: moderate: depends on the caterer's quote
corporate.note: A lighter meal helps attention after lunch.

corporate.title: Test the sound, display and internet at the venue before the day
corporate.note: Technical surprises cost the most time on the day.

corporate.title: A feedback card or quick poll at the end
corporate.note: Gives the organiser real input for next time.

corporate.title: Clear signage from the entrance to the room
corporate.note: Saves staff from answering directions all morning.

corporate.title: Mark vegetarian dishes clearly on the buffet
corporate.note: Clear marking helps attendees choose quickly.

corporate.title: Keep a short list of who is speaking and for how long
corporate.note: A written run order keeps sessions on time.

conference.title: Set up a registration desk with printed name badges ready before doors open
conference.cost_note: low to moderate, depending on printing
conference.note: Badges and a desk prevent a queue at the start.

conference.title: One short theme line used on the programme, badges and signage
conference.note: A single line ties materials together.

conference.title: A networking break with a few conversation prompts on the tables
Brief each speaker on timing, microphones and slides the day before
Ask the caterer for tea and snack breaks placed between sessions
conference.cost_note: moderate: depends on the caterer's quote
conference.note: Breaks that match the programme keep rooms full.

conference.title: Mark vegetarian options on every food station
Ask the venue about step-free routes and quiet spaces and write down the answers
conference.note: Attendees often need to know before they come.

conference.title: A feedback poll shared as people leave
conference.note: Collects input while it is fresh.

other.title: Choose one colour and one word that describe the mood of the day
other.note: A tiny brief keeps decisions consistent.

other.title: String lights and a simple backdrop for photos
other.note: Easy to set up and good in photographs.

other.title: One group activity near the start so people mix
other.note: Early mixing helps the rest of the day.

other.title: Write the running order on one page and share it with everyone helping
Ask the caterer to label dishes clearly
other.note: Clear labels help guests with different diets.

other.title: Plan a weather backup if any part is outdoors
other.note: Outdoor plans depend on the weather.

other.title: Choose one person to answer questions on the day
A short thank-you moment near the end
other.note: Ends the day on a warm note.

community.title: Write a one-page volunteer brief: what the day is, who does what, and who to call
community.note: A short brief makes it easier to recruit and keep volunteers.

community.title: Ask each volunteer for one hour of help rather than a whole day, so more people can say yes
community.note: Shorter shifts widen the pool of helpers.

community.title: Make a simple publicity checklist: poster, group chats, notice boards and one personal invitation each
community.note: A checklist keeps outreach from depending on one person.

community.title: Pick one welcoming line for the posters and the stage, in the languages your community uses
community.note: One clear line helps everyone feel invited.

community.title: A single hand-painted welcome board at the entrance made by local students or members
community.note: Local hands make the entrance feel like the community's own.

community.title: A short thank-you moment for volunteers before the event closes
community.note: Recognition is the easiest way to keep volunteers for next time.

community.title: Plan where people can sit and rest, and mark a quiet corner
community.note: A crowd includes people who tire quickly.

community.title: Ask the caterer about simple, easy-to-serve food that keeps queues short
community.cost_note: moderate: depends on the caterer's quote
community.note: Short queues matter at community events.

college_fest.title: A student-run stage slot sign-up so performers apply in advance
college_fest.note: Advance sign-up keeps the programme realistic.

college_fest.title: Ask the college which departments or clubs can lend volunteers and equipment
college_fest.note: Clubs already organise people and tools.

college_fest.title: Department-themed corners that students decorate themselves
college_fest.note: Ownership by students keeps costs and effort spread out.

college_fest.title: Write sponsor note wording: the cause, the date, the audience and what sponsors can expect
college_fest.note: Short, clear wording makes sponsor conversations easier.

neighbourhood_gathering.title: A potluck-style table where each household brings one dish and a label
neighbourhood_gathering.note: Shared food spreads the cost and the work.

neighbourhood_gathering.title: A children's corner run by two or three parents in shifts
neighbourhood_gathering.note: Parents can enjoy the event if children are looked after.

neighbourhood_gathering.title: Ask the residents' group which common areas and equipment members can use
neighbourhood_gathering.note: The group usually knows what is on hand.

neighbourhood_gathering.title: Tell neighbours about timing and noise a week ahead with a short notice
neighbourhood_gathering.note: Advance notice avoids surprises for nearby homes.

fundraiser.title: Write a one-paragraph story of the cause that every volunteer can repeat
fundraiser.note: A shared story keeps the message consistent.

fundraiser.title: Draft sponsor outreach wording: who you are, what the money is for, and how sponsors will be thanked
fundraiser.note: Clear wording helps sponsors decide quickly.

fundraiser.title: A visible progress board that shows what has been raised so far
Plan how every contribution will be recorded and acknowledged, with a second person present
fundraiser.note: Two people and a written record protect everyone involved.

cultural_festival_local.title: Invite local groups to each present a short piece, with a fixed time for each
cultural_festival_local.note: Fixed slots keep a varied programme on time.

cultural_festival_local.title: Ask community elders and organisers how the day is usually run and who should be consulted
cultural_festival_local.note: The people who know the community's own practice should guide it.

cultural_festival_local.title: Display boards where each group can share a short story about its work
cultural_festival_local.note: Gives visitors something to read between performances.

cultural_festival_local.title: Plan clear walking routes and signage for visitors and performers
cultural_festival_local.note: A clear route reduces crowding at doors.

other.title: Agree one sentence that says what the event is for, and use it on every poster and message
other.note: A single purpose keeps the programme focused.

other.title: A short welcome by the organisers that names the helpers
